newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel says seeks to maintain market share.
newsitem.headline: Opel says seeks to maintain market share.

text.p: German carmaker Adam Opel AG, the German unit of General Motors Corp, said on Thursday it expected an improvement in vehicle deliveries during the second half of 1997 and to maintain 1996 market share levels.
"Our goal in Germany and Europe is to maintain our market share from last year," Opel managing director David Herman said in a statement at the carmaker's annual news conference.
Herman said Opel expected 1997 sales of about 30 billion marks, which would set a new record.
He said the sales growth would occur despite his expectations for little expansion in the German and European vehicle markets.
Herman said the German vehicle market should have 3.5 million new vehicle sales and the European market about 13.1 million vehicles.
